answer: Rank identities by how often random walks from trusted seeds land on them. Walks follow real endorsements, so a genuine agent sits near the trusted core, while a clone farm hangs off a few bought links: walks rarely cross that thin thread into the farm, so its whole rank collapses together. A new clone adds almost nothing unless the attacker buys genuine bridges into the core, each costing real relationships. The summit thus belongs to well-connected agents, and each vertex is judged by its neighbourhood, not its claims. Limit: seed choice biases rankings, and newcomers start low.
